audit.title: Research-grade biosignal workflow
audit.disclaimer: Study Runner is a research tool. It is not a medical device and produces no diagnosis.
audit.sensors.title: Sensors
audit.sensors.body: EEG, heart and breathing rate, and camera-based emotion estimates are recorded as separate streams and never merged into a single score.
audit.timing.title: Timing
audit.timing.body: LSL timestamps are the reference clock. Tablet events carry their own clock offset so browser and sensor time can be compared honestly.
audit.data.title: Data
audit.data.body: Raw values are kept. Camera frames are analysed and discarded; no video is ever stored. Results are written crash-safe before any upload is attempted.
audit.limits.title: Limits
audit.limits.body: Emotion estimates are model output, not ground truth. Wireless sensors can drop samples; gaps are recorded rather than interpolated.
audit.workflow.title: Lab workflow
audit.workflow.step1: Check every sensor on the dashboard before the participant arrives.
audit.workflow.step2: Load the study, select a waiting device if several are connected, then press Play.
audit.workflow.step3: Watch the live status during the session; interruptions are recorded, not hidden.
audit.workflow.step4: After the session, verify the saved files and the upload state before clearing the room.

pluginHelp.notion.intro:
Study Runner writes a short summary of every finished session into a Notion database. You need three things:

- an **API key** from a Notion integration,
- a **Notion page** that the integration may use,
- the **ID of that page**.

The full data always stays on this computer. Notion only receives the summary.

After filling in the fields, press **Test connection**. It tells you exactly what is still wrong.
pluginHelp.notion.apiKey:
**What is it?** A secret key that allows Study Runner to write into your Notion workspace.

**Where do I get it?**

- Open **notion.so/profile/integrations** in the browser.
- Click **New integration**, give it a name (e.g. "Study Runner"), choose your workspace, and save.
- Copy the **Internal integration secret**. It starts with `ntn_` or `secret_`.
- Paste it here and press **Save credential for this study**.

**Typical mistake:** copying the integration ID instead of the secret, or a space at the start or end.
pluginHelp.notion.parentPageId:
**What is it?** The Notion page under which Study Runner creates its results database.

**Where do I get it?**

- Create or open a page in Notion, e.g. "Study results".
- Share it with the integration: click **•••** at the top right, then **Connections**, then add your integration. **Without this step Notion refuses every upload.**
- Click **Share > Copy link**. The link ends with 32 letters and numbers - that is the ID.
- Example: in `notion.so/Study-results-1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2f3a4b5c6d` the ID is `1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2f3a4b5c6d`.

You can paste the whole link; Study Runner reads the ID from it.
pluginHelp.notion.databaseId:
**What is it?** An existing Notion database for the results.

**Usually: leave it empty.** Study Runner then creates the database under the parent page by itself and fills in this field.

Only fill it in if you want to reuse a database that already exists. Open the database as a full page and copy the 32 characters from its link, like for the parent page. The database must also be shared with the integration (••• > Connections).
pluginHelp.notion.dataSourceId: You do not need to enter anything here. Study Runner fills this in by itself after the first successful upload.

pluginHelp.nextcloud.intro:
Study Runner copies every finished session folder into a Nextcloud folder, as a backup. You need a **public share link** to that folder that allows uploading.

After filling in the fields, press **Test connection**.
pluginHelp.nextcloud.shareLink:
**What is it?** A link to a Nextcloud folder that Study Runner may upload into.

**Where do I get it?**

- In Nextcloud, create a folder, e.g. "Study results".
- Click the **share** icon next to the folder and add a **Share link**.
- In the link settings, allow **uploading / editing** ("Allow upload and editing" or "File drop").
- Copy the link. It looks like `https://cloud.example.org/s/AbCdEf123`.

**Typical mistake:** a read-only link. Then the connection test succeeds, but uploads fail.
pluginHelp.nextcloud.password:
**What is it?** The password of the share link - only if you set one in Nextcloud.

**Where do I get it?** In the link settings of the share in Nextcloud ("Password protect").

If the link has no password, leave this empty.

pluginHelp.amHub.intro: Connects Study Runner to a Parasite AM Hub on the local network. Set the hub URL, then verify live data on the dashboard.

pluginHelp.amHub.timestampCorrection: Off (default): each sample keeps the time it arrived at this computer, and the estimated latency is recorded in latency_ms. On: the timestamp becomes the arrival time minus the estimated latency (board to hub by radio, hub to Study Runner), clamped to never move backwards; correction_ms records what was actually taken off, so the arrival time can always be rebuilt from the XDF. Applies after the AM Hub is restarted.

cards.moodMeter.help.title: Mood Meter views
cards.moodMeter.help.intro: All four views use the same word lists and the same two dimensions: **energy** (bottom to top) and **pleasantness** (left to right). The default words are Brackett's original 10 x 10 Mood Meter grid, read row by row, so every word sits where the Mood Meter puts it.
cards.moodMeter.help.classic: The Mood Meter of the RULER approach: four colored quadrants, then all words on a plane the participant can pan. Records the chosen words.
cards.moodMeter.help.blobs: The same four quadrants as breathing shapes, after the shape language of the How We Feel app: jagged for high-energy unpleasant, flowering for high-energy pleasant, soft for calm, hanging for low. A tap grows the shape into the word space. Records the chosen words.
cards.moodMeter.help.field: An Affect Grid: the participant places one point on pleasantness x energy by dragging a light whose shape follows the feeling (as in Apple's State of Mind). The nearest words appear around it. Records the chosen words and the point.
cards.moodMeter.help.orbit: The circumplex of affect as a wheel, read like the Geneva Emotion Wheel: the angle is the kind of feeling, the distance from the middle its intensity. Words near the finger grow. Records the chosen words, the point and the intensity.
cards.moodMeter.help.data: Field and orbit add `pleasantness` and `energy` from 0 to 1 (0.5 is neutral) to the answer, orbit also `intensity` (0 = middle, 1 = rim). To compare with the 9-point Affect Grid use `1 + 8 * value`.
pluginHelp.destination.enabled: Off means this computer uploads nothing to this destination; studies that use it show a warning before they start.
pluginHelp.destination.timeoutSeconds: How long one network request may take before it counts as failed. Raise it for slow connections.
pluginHelp.destination.autoRetry: On: a failed upload is tried again by itself (after 30 s, 2 min, 10 min, 30 min, then hourly). Off: it waits until you press Retry in the session's progress rail. The data stays saved locally either way.
pluginHelp.destination.retryHours: How long automatic retries continue before the upload is marked as failed (1-168 hours).
